instruction: Create a folder named 'receipts' in your home directory and move the image OIP.jpg into it.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened file manager, found OIP.jpg, opened terminal, tried ImageMagick convert with wrong filename (QIP.jpg instead of OIP.jpg), installed imagemagick, still failed due to filename error and policy restrictions, eventually opened image in Image Viewer and tried Print to File but ran out of turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open file manager, open terminal, run shell commands (ls, cp, mv, apt install, find, mkdir), install packages with sudo, open images in Image Viewer, interact with Print dialog, navigate folders in dialogs
metadata.failure_analysis: Model misread filename as QIP.jpg instead of OIP.jpg, wasted many turns on wrong convert commands. ImageMagick also had policy restrictions. Eventually found correct filename but ran out of 50 turns before completing the print-to-file approach.
metadata.task_rationale: Two-step file organization task: create directory + move file. The model demonstrated ability to use mkdir and mv commands. This tests both directory creation and file movement, with partial credit allowing the model to score even if it only completes one step.
metadata.explanation: Task requires creating /home/user/receipts/ directory and moving OIP.jpg into it. Custom getter checks directory existence and file presence. Custom metric provides 0.5 partial credit for directory creation and 0.5 for file move.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly checks /home/user/receipts directory existence and /home/user/receipts/OIP.jpg file presence via bash scripts, matching the instruction requirements exactly.
Metric correctly provides partial credit: 0.5 for directory creation + 0.5 for file move, covering both instruction steps.
No postconfig needed since file system state persists without UI dependencies.
Minor: expected rules (dir_name, file_name) are not used by the metric; paths are hardcoded in the getter. Functionally correct but not parameterized.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider having the getter read dir_name and file_name from the config rules instead of hardcoding paths, for better reusability.
